# myjfrog_private_link (Resource)

Provides a MyJFrog [PrivateLink](https://jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-hosting-models-documentation/configure-privatelink-for-jfrog-cloud) resource to manage PrivateLink connections for JFrog cloud instances.

->This resource is supported only on the Cloud (SaaS) platform.

~>The PrivateLink API does not support in-place updates. Changing `private_link_id` or `server_names` forces replacement of the resource (delete and recreate).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "myjfrog_private_link" "myjfrog-private-link" {
  private_link_id = "pl-abc123def456"
  server_names = [
    "myserver",
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `private_link_id` (String) Unique identifier for the PrivateLink connection. This value is used as the Terraform resource ID.
- `server_names` (List of String) List of JFrog server names to associate with the PrivateLink connection. If your JFrog URL is `myserver.jfrog.io`, the server name is `myserver`. Changing this value forces replacement of the resource, as the API does not support in-place updates.

### Read-Only

- `servers` (Attributes List) List of servers and their PrivateLink status values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--servers))

<a id="nestedatt--servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `servers`

Read-Only:

- `server_name` (String)
- `status` (String) PrivateLink status value. One of: `connected`, `connecting`, `removing`, `FAILED (not found)`, `FAILED (internal issue)`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import myjfrog_private_link.myjfrog-private-link pl-abc123def456
```
